title: Two Foolish Goats
subject: English Language
objectives: Read and understand a cautionary tale about pride

blocks.alt: Two goats on a log over a stream
blocks.caption: Two goats met in the middle of a log bridge.

blocks.md:
Two goats were running away from their greedy masters and met each other in the middle of the log of wood that the villagers on either side of the stream used as a bridge. None of them wanted to go back as they found it difficult to walk backwards. They were not wise enough to think on how to cross that narrow log. Then they started to argue.

'I got here first,' said one.

'Really, I got here first,' shouted the other.

'Give way,' said one.

'No, you give way,' replied the other.

'If you don't move, I will push you,' said one.

'Try and see,' bleated the other.

'I will kick you,' threatened one.

'And I will crack you,' shouted the other.

None was ready to give way. And then they started to fight with each other. The log of wood was not wide enough for both of them to walk at a time and so they fell into the stream. As the goats were not good swimmers, they both drowned.
**The Lesson:** Always be willing to compromise. Pride and stubbornness can lead to destruction.

quiz.q: What were the two goats running away from?
quiz.explain: They were running away from their greedy masters.
They met in the middle of the log of wood used as a bridge.

quiz.q: Why did neither goat want to go back?
quiz.explain: They found it difficult to walk backwards on the narrow log.

quiz.q: What happened to both of them?
quiz.explain: They both fell into the stream and drowned because they couldn't swim.

quiz.q: What is the lesson of this story?
options: Always fight for what you want
quiz.explain: The story teaches us that stubbornness can lead to destruction.
